uncited: - A lattice in world space consisting of $c$ sections, where each section is defined by four corner curves.
- **Corner Curves:** Four sets of control points defining the cross-section at each lattice section.

**Sample Center Curve Properties:** For each control point $P_i$, determine the parameter $t$ at which that control point has the most influence.
**Generate Corner Curves:** Generate four additional curves by placing control points on the corners of these squares.
**Evaluate Corner Positions:** For each of the $c$ sampled $t$ values, evaluate the four corner curves using Equation (6) to obtain $c$ sets of correlated positions on the four corner curves.
- **Inverse Parameterization:** The pixel shader operates on deformed world space $P'$ to return texture space $P$, but the deformation function $D(P)$ defines $P'$ from $P$.
This cannot be solved analytically on the GPU.
- **Pixel Coverage:** The shader can only render to locations occupied by triangle fragments.
The final pixel coverage is not known a priori.
- **Discontinuities:** Linear interpolation on the lattice creates discontinuities in the first derivative of the curve on the borders of each lattice section.
- **Time Complexity:** The lattice construction is $O(c \cdot n)$, where $c$ is the lattice resolution and $n$ is the number of control points.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(c \cdot n)$ for storing the lattice vertices and control points.
